results.text: On 05-Oct-2026 I was at my shop in Malegaon the whole day, from 10 in the morning till 9 at night. I did not go to Nashik that day. My debit card is always with me and nobody else uses it.

results.text: Narmada Bank, Malegaon branch, Nashik district. Reply to notice under Section 94 BNSS dated 08-Oct-2026. Account No. 31082290447, current account in the name of "Shaikh Mobile Point", proprietor Imran Rafiq Shaikh, age 27, Kidwai Road, Malegaon. Registered mobile 9890447120.

results.text: Arrest memo 2: Imran Rafiq Shaikh, age 27, Malegaon, arrested on 15-Oct-2026 at 13:05 hrs at Malegaon by PSI Akash Shinde in FIR 114/2026. Grounds of arrest explained. Information of arrest given to his wife at 13:20 hrs. Medical examination done at General Hospital, Malegaon.

events.text:
Imran Shaikh's phone (9890447120) went from Malegaon to Nashik and back on the afternoon of 5 October 2026. Between 14:21 and 15:08 it was on the Dwarka Circle, Nashik tower, which is when six ATM withdrawals were made from his account at an ATM at Dwarka Circle. This goes against his statement that he was at his shop in Malegaon all day and did not go to Nashik (DOC-14 ¶4).

**Where the phone was, step by step:**
- **12:35:** Kidwai Road, Malegaon, where his shop is (CDR 9890447120, tower MLG-KDW-01)
- **13:22:** Chandwad, Nashik district, a highway tower between Malegaon and Nashik (NSK-HWY-05)
- **14:21 to 15:08:** Dwarka Circle, Nashik, 5 records (NSK-DWK-02)
- **16:10:** Chandwad again, so heading back (NSK-HWY-05)
- **17:32:** Kidwai Road, Malegaon (MLG-KDW-01)

**Money moved from his account (31082290447) in the same window:**
- Six ATM withdrawals at ATM NB-NSK-0417, Dwarka Circle, Nashik, between 14:31 and 14:43, totalling Rs 2,97,000 (TXN T00022–T00027).
- At 15:20, Rs 9,40,000 went by IMPS to "Gulshan Traders", account 6620045519, marked "supplier payment" (TXN T00028). This is the next layer to trace.

**Limits of this evidence:**
- Tower records show where the SIM was, not who was carrying it. His card was used at that ATM while his phone was on that tower, and he says nobody else uses his card (DOC-14 ¶4). That makes it more likely he was there, but it doesn't prove it.
- Before confronting him, check the ATM CCTV note (DOC-21) to see who is actually on camera at the machine. I haven't read it yet.
- Also check whether his handset (IMEI) or Sameer Ansari's phone (9765330812) was at Dwarka Circle at the same time. I can run either check if you want.

results.title: Search and seizure panchnama at the house of Sameer Ansari, Nashik
results.text: Articles seized: (1) black smartphone, IMEI 356938112847152, with SIM 9765330812 inserted; (2) a basic keypad phone, IMEI 861234055591027, without SIM; (3) three loose SIM cards including one Trinet SIM whose ICCID matches the SIM issued for 8969204117; (4) a printed fake identity card in the name "Vikram Rathore, Deputy Superintendent, CBI"; (5) a khaki uniform shirt with shoulder badges; (6) Rs 4,80,000 in cash in a cupboard.

events.text:
The records point to **Sameer Ansari (9765330812, Bhadrakali, Nashik)** as the person using 8969204117, the "CBI Vikram Rathore" number. The SIM was registered with fake KYC in the name Ramesh Yadav. The strongest link is the phone itself: Ansari's own SIM and the scam SIM were used one after the other in the same handset, and that handset was seized from his house. This is evidence of who used the number. His exact role and who else was involved still need to be established.

**Evidence:**
- **Same handset:** Phone IMEI 356938112847152 ran Ansari's SIM 9765330812 until 29-Sep 23:48. It ran the scam SIM 8969204117 from 30-Sep 08:05 to 06-Oct 21:14, which is the whole period of the fraud. Ansari's SIM went back in from 07-Oct 09:31, the morning after the complaint was made on 06-Oct. (DOC-09 ¶2; the CDR handset check matches, showing 76 events of 8969204117 on this IMEI only.)
- **Seizure:** That handset was found at Ansari's house with his SIM 9765330812 inside it. A loose Trinet SIM whose ICCID (SIM card serial number) matches the one issued for 8969204117 was also found there, along with a printed fake "Vikram Rathore, Deputy Superintendent, CBI" ID card, a khaki uniform shirt and Rs 4,80,000 in cash. (DOC-18 ¶3)
- **Video-call account:** The ConnectX account "cbi.vikram.rathore" was created on 29-Sep-2026 and verified with 8969204117. (DOC-10 ¶2)
- **Forensic report:** The seized handset is logged in to that ConnectX account. Its call history shows video calls to "Prof K Kothrud" on 3, 4 and 5 Oct. Its gallery has a fake CBI ID image and a fake arrest warrant. (DOC-20 ¶2)
- **"Courier" number too:** A keypad phone seized from Ansari (IMEI 861234055591027) is the only handset ever used with the courier number 7303518246. Its call log shows calls to the victim (9822041763) on 03-Oct from 10:12. (DOC-09 ¶4, DOC-20 ¶4, DOC-18 ¶3)

**Still open:**
- **Who else used the phone:** The handset records cannot show whether anyone else handled it. Ansari's statement and a check of his CDR against Imran Shaikh's and Rohit Pawar's numbers would help settle this.
- **Where the scam SIM was used:** Comparing the tower locations of 8969204117 with Ansari's own number around 30-Sep and 07-Oct would show whether the scam SIM was used from his area.
- **Who supplied the SIM:** The Trinet CAF (customer application form) and the retailer's details for the "Ramesh Yadav" SIM should be checked to find who arranged the fake-KYC SIM.

events.text: I should also check contacts for Rohit, Imran, and Sameer in parallel.

The records so far do not link Anil Kulkarni to the fraud. The family's suspicion rests on him having stayed with them and helped set up banking, plus an old loan. The phone records and his employer's records support his statement that he was in Bengaluru during the fraud, and his number had no contact with any suspect or layer number.

**Evidence**
- **Why the family suspects him:** He stayed with them in Kothrud from 20 to 28 September and set up the victim's net banking app. Mrs. Kulkarni also points to an unpaid Rs 2 lakh loan (DOC-05 ¶3, DOC-03 ¶2). He admits both but says he kept no password and has repaid Rs 1.2 lakh (DOC-15 ¶2, ¶4). That repayment has not been checked yet.
- **Where his phone was during the fraud:** On 3–4 October his phone used the Brookefield, Bengaluru tower. On 5–6 October it used the Whitefield tower, then Brookefield in the evening. It never showed in Pune or Nashik (location timeline for 9845012377, 3–6 October).
- **Employer records:** His access card was swiped at the Whitefield office on 5 October (09:12–19:40) and 6 October (09:05–18:55). Leave ended on 28 September, and 3–4 October were weekly offs (DOC-16 ¶2–3). This matches his statement (DOC-15 ¶3) and the tower data.
- **No calls or SMS with any suspect number:** His records show nothing with the "CBI" number 8969204117, the "courier" number 7303518246, Sameer Ansari (9765330812), Imran Shaikh (9890447120) or Rohit Pawar (9371662405).
- **One handset only:** His SIM ran in a single phone (IMEI 357201093361845) from 1 September to 8 October, so there is no sign of SIM-swapping.
- **Evidence points elsewhere:** The OTPs went from Rohit Pawar to 8969204117, a number given to him by Imran Shaikh (DOC-22 ¶4). Sameer Ansari's phone holds OTP SMSs from Rohit and a chat with "Imran Mlg" about the cash withdrawals (DOC-20 ¶3). Anil does not appear anywhere in this chain.

**Limits: what would close the point**
- Being in Bengaluru does not rule out remote help, such as passing on the uncle's bank details. To check this:
  - Look up his handset IMEI 357201093361845 to confirm no scam SIM ever ran in it.
  - Check whether his number or name appears in the contacts or chats on Sameer Ansari's seized phones (DOC-20).
  - Get his bank statement through a Section 94 BNSS notice to look for any money received after 3 October.
- Ask the victim's bank for login and device logs of his net banking. This would show whether any login came from a device other than his own.

Unless those checks turn up something, the records indicate Anil Kulkarni can be shown in the case diary as examined, with nothing found against him so far.

events.text:
I traced all Rs 38.5 lakh. It went into Rohit Pawar's account, and within minutes almost all of it was sent on to three accounts: Imran Shaikh (Rs 21.4 lakh), Bapi Mondal (Rs 8.6 lakh) and Hemant Saini (Rs 8.4 lakh). Most of it then left as cash or moved further. **Rs 10.3 lakh is frozen so far.** About Rs 18.97 lakh was taken out as cash in Nashik and Kolkata, and Rs 8.4 lakh moved on into wallets that haven't been traced.

**Account 1: Victim, Sahyadri National Bank a/c 10020034571**
- Three RTGS transfers made at the branch, all to Rohit Pawar's account 50210043318876, totalling Rs 38,50,000:
  - 03-Oct 15:40: Rs 9,50,000 (TXN T00001)
  - 03-Oct 17:05: Rs 12,00,000 (TXN T00003)
  - 05-Oct 11:20: Rs 17,00,000 (TXN T00005)

**Account 2: Rohit Pawar, Konkan SFB a/c 50210043318876 (first layer)**
- Each RTGS was moved out by IMPS within 10–35 minutes:
  - **To Imran Shaikh:** Rs 21,40,000 in five transfers of Rs 4.9L, 4.9L, 3.1L, 4.9L and 3.6L (TXN T00007, T00010, T00013, T00015, T00017).
  - **To Bapi Mondal:** Rs 8,60,000 in two transfers of Rs 4.6L and 4.0L on 03-Oct (TXN T00009, T00012).
  - **To Hemant Saini:** Rs 8,40,000 on 05-Oct 11:40 (TXN T00019).
- These add up to Rs 38.4 lakh. The rows I pulled don't show where the last Rs 10,000 went; check the closing balance and freeze status in the Konkan SFB reply (DOC-06).
- Before this, the account only showed small student spending. It also received **Rs 15,000 from Imran Shaikh's account on 27-Sep, marked "acct rent"** (TXN T00021). This points to the account having been rented out and links Rohit and Imran before the fraud. Put this to both of them.

**Account 3a: Imran Shaikh, Narmada Bank a/c 31082290447 (second layer)**
- Received Rs 21.4 lakh and emptied it within about a day:
  - **ATM cash:** Rs 2,97,000 in six withdrawals at ATM NB-NSK-0417, Dwarka Circle, Nashik, on 05-Oct between 14:31 and 14:43 (TXN T00022–T00027). This ATM is the subject of the CCTV note, DOC-21.
  - **To Gulshan Traders, Ulhasnagar (a/c 6620045519):** Rs 9,40,000 by IMPS on 05-Oct 15:20, marked "supplier payment" (TXN T00028).
  - **Self-cheque cash withdrawal:** Rs 9,00,000 at the Nashik Road branch on 06-Oct 12:15 (TXN T00029).
- The account was debit-frozen on 06-Oct at 16:30 with only Rs 3,120 left (DOC-07 ¶5).

**Account 3b: Bapi Mondal, Bengal Rural Bank, Kolkata, a/c 7700118245**
- Received Rs 8.6 lakh. Rs 4.2 lakh is under lien; the rest was taken out at Kolkata ATMs on 04-Oct (DOC-11 ¶2).

**Account 3c: Hemant Saini, Marudhar Co-op Bank, Jaipur, a/c 0451200381**
- Received Rs 8.4 lakh. Balance was nil when frozen; the money had gone on to several wallets, and that enquiry is still pending (DOC-11 ¶3).

**Account 4: Gulshan Traders, Ulhasnagar, a/c 6620045519 (third layer)**
- Received Rs 9.4 lakh. Rs 6.1 lakh is under lien since 07-Oct (DOC-11 ¶4).

**Where the money stands**

| Status | Amount |
|---|---|
| Frozen (Rs 4.2L Bapi Mondal + Rs 6.1L Gulshan Traders) | Rs 10.3 lakh (DOC-11 ¶5) |
| Cash: Nashik ATM Rs 2.97L + Nashik Road self-cheque Rs 9.0L + Kolkata ATMs about Rs 4.4L | about Rs 16.4 lakh |
| Gulshan Traders balance not under lien (Rs 9.4L − 6.1L) | Rs 3.3 lakh, not traced |
| Moved on from Hemant Saini to wallets | Rs 8.4 lakh, not traced |

**Gaps and suggested next notices**
- **Section 94 BNSS notices to the wallet providers** for Hemant Saini's onward transfers.
- **Gulshan Traders' full statement and KYC**, to follow the Rs 3.3 lakh not under lien and to test the "supplier payment" label.
- **Narmada Bank, Nashik Road branch:** CCTV and the withdrawal slip for self-cheque 000117, to see who collected the Rs 9 lakh.
- **Bengal Rural Bank:** ATM IDs and CCTV for the 04-Oct Kolkata withdrawals.
- **Examine Bapi Mondal and Hemant Saini;** neither has been questioned yet (DOC-11 ¶5).

The records show the money passing through these accounts. They don't by themselves show who controlled each one.

events.text:
The case diary and documents on file still leave several gaps. The main ones are three missing Section 63 BSA certificates, the final forensic report, a confirmed identity for the man who came with Rohit Pawar, the unexamined layer-account holders, and a decision on Anil Kulkarni. Until these are filled, key electronic evidence may not be admissible and the account of who did what is not complete.

**Evidence and certificates still missing**
- **ATM CCTV certificate:** We rely on the Dwarka Circle, Nashik ATM footage to identify the accused, but the bank has not yet sent the Section 63 BSA certificate. Chase Narmada Bank for it (DOC-21 ¶4; DOC-23 ¶4).
- **Final forensic report on Sameer Ansari's phones:** The report on file is only preliminary. The full extraction and its Section 63 certificate will come with the final report (DOC-20 ¶5). The phones were not hashed when seized; the lab hashed them on receipt with seals intact (DOC-18 ¶4; DOC-20 ¶1). Be ready to explain this sequence in court.
- **Konkan SFB branch CCTV (25-Sep) and identification:** The branch manager has preserved the footage and says he can identify the man who came with Rohit Pawar. We still need to collect the footage with its certificate and hold an identification (TIP) (DOC-13 ¶4). Rohit Pawar has offered to repeat his statement before a Magistrate; record it under s.183 BNSS (DOC-22 ¶5).

**Money trail still open (only Rs 10.3 lakh of Rs 38.5 lakh frozen)**
- **Bapi Mondal (Kolkata) and Hemant Saini (Jaipur):** Neither has been examined. Rs 8.6 lakh went to Mondal; the money not under lien was withdrawn at Kolkata ATMs. Saini's Rs 8.4 lakh moved on to several wallets, and that enquiry is still pending. We need s.94 BNSS notices to the wallet companies, plus ATM CCTV from Kolkata (DOC-11 ¶2, ¶3, ¶5).
- **Gulshan Traders, Ulhasnagar:** It received Rs 9.4 lakh from Imran Shaikh's account and Rs 6.1 lakh is under lien. I found no examination of this account holder on file (DOC-11 ¶4).

**Other gaps**
- **Who used 8969204117 and 7303518246:** The ConnectX account "cbi.vikram.rathore" is logged in on Sameer Ansari's phone (DOC-20 ¶2), and the platform's logins trace to the Nashik telecom circle (DOC-10 ¶3). The two SIMs were issued on false identities through point-of-sale agents in Malegaon and Nashik (DOC-23 ¶3). I found no statements from those agents and no customer application forms (CAFs) with photos or fingerprints. These would tie the SIMs to a real person.
- **Imran Shaikh's denial:** He says he does not know Rohit Pawar and the Rs 15,000 sent on 27-Sep may have been his staff's mistake (DOC-14 ¶3). Sameer's phone has a chat with "Imran Mlg" about card withdrawals, which points the other way (DOC-20 ¶3). For the chargesheet, back this link with CDR and transaction records.
- **Anil Kulkarni:** His aunt Vandana named him as a suspect (DOC-05 ¶4). His statement and employer letter are on file (DOC-15, DOC-16), but I have not checked them against his CDR. Record a clear finding either way.

I did not run the CDR, IMEI or transaction cross-checks for this answer. The case diary I found only runs to 10-Oct, and those analyses were listed as pending then (DOC-23 ¶5). If you want, I can run them now to confirm the phone and money links for the chargesheet.
